problems: The mud and green verge meet along uninterrupted straight boundaries, making the track feel engineered despite having no kerbs.
In the assembled scene, identical oval puddles, round vegetation patches and footprints repeat at conspicuous intervals, creating an accidental landscaped border.

The mud track has perfectly straight, parallel edges, and the |z| 4–6 strip is a uniform darker-green band with straight edges on both sides. In the vignette this reads exactly as a road with two sidewalks, which is what Sami said must not exist.

The dressing repeats identically on every 16 m tile: the same two teal puddles with dark rims and the same pale tufts 1.7 m wide. Along the corner they appear at even spacing, like manholes or planted roundels.
The puddles' dark mud rim plus teal top reads as a crisp disc, not a puddle.
On the verges, the pale-yellow disc (~1.2 m) and the light-green disc look like flat stickers or lily pads, not moss or trampled grass
The two dark 'drag grooves' render as black slits or holes in the mud, not shallow ruts
The puddles are flat teal ellipses with no rim, and they read as decals
The middle of the road is empty apart from faint footprint texture, so the track has no ruts that would sell 'trampled sledge track'

Render it with the countryside meadow surface (no separate verge surface). Require the street dressing to include at least 5 mud-spill or tussock parts straddling z = ±4, so the track edge is ragged and the mud bleeds into the grass.

World rule: roads/street dressing: forbid flat pale-yellow or light-green discs on the verges (they read as stickers). Ground details must be darker than or close to their surface, or be raised lumps. Drag grooves should be paired parallel ruts in #533d30, not black slits.

Shrink the pale #a8ad68 tuft cone to ≤0.9 m wide and recolour it #7c9254. Make the puddles irregular by overlapping 2–3 flat spheres of different sizes per puddle, and drop the dark rim ring. Replace the two black slits with two long parallel shallow ruts along x (boxes 5–7 m long, 0.35 m wide, 0.03 m tall, #533d30), offset ±1.2 m from the centre, with a thin lighter ridge (#987052) between them. problems: The birch has a straight pole trunk and compact centred ball crown.
The pine is a tidy stack of nearly centred cones, not a shorter crooked tree with one heavy side.
These silhouettes directly contradict Sami's requirement for wild, irregular surviving growth.

Birch: six sphere crown masses packed into one round ball on a trunk tilted only about 8°. It is a lollipop tree, not the 'leaning birch with a torn, sparse crown' the bible asks for. The uniformly cream trunk with neat evenly spaced black bands looks manufactured.
Pine: three centred cones stacked on a straight trunk give a symmetric Christmas-tree outline. The 'one heavy side' is a single small cone that is barely visible.
Together they look like two deliberately planted ornamental trees on a verge, which is exactly the 'too normal and symmetrical' look Sami flagged.
The pine is three stacked, centred cones plus a side cone: a symmetric Christmas tree, exactly what Sami's note rejects
The birch crown is a dense round cluster of unrotated spheres, which reads as a broccoli or lollipop crown on a straight pale stick
Both trees have roughly equal-sized foliage masses, so the 'one heavy side' and 'torn, sparse crown' of the bible do not show

World rule: trees: add a hard rule that every foliage mass must overlap a trunk or branch part (no floating foliage), and that no single tree may have its foliage centroid within 0.5 m of its trunk base in x/z (forces lean or one heavy side).

Ban single small spheres hanging at twig ends. Ban stacked centred cones for pines: tiers must be offset to one side, tilted, of unequal size, with a broken or bare top. Give each tree a minimum foliage volume so it reads at stream scale.

Build it mostly from spheres: a high domed head, a back sloping down to the rump, a hanging fur skirt of cones to the knees, dark brown #6b4a32 with ginger highlights, shoulder about 3 m. Forbid box-stack bodies and flat sienna/orange slabs.
World rule: arrival/camp mammoth: specify a dark base fur (#6b3a22), a trunk in a darker distinct tone, a head hump and a hanging shaggy fringe, so the mammoth does not read as an orange box robot.
elements.fix: Reallocate the 72 parts to a windbreak of leaning unequal branches, a few crossing limbs and visible hide lashings; remove the regular green caps. Give the resting mammoth an uneven shaggy outline and keep the two tents, fire, sledge and contrasting flint-and-hide bundles clearly separated. / Use the shared sphere-based mammoth build (see arrival), lying down with its legs tucked under and the fur skirt pooling on the ground. Rebuild the windbreak as 6–8 leaning branches (cylinders tilted 0.3–0.6 rad, crossed) with 2–3 flat irregular brush clumps woven in at different heights, never one sphere per post. Make the A-frame tent hide on poles: let 2–3 crossed pole tips stick out above the ridge, sag the hide panels (split each into 2 slightly offset slabs), and add a dark doorway gap. / Rebuild the windbreak as 5–6 leaning brush bundles (sticks at 0.3–0.5 rad with dense #526b40 brushwood boxes along their length, not caps on top), 1.8 m tall, curved behind the tents. Apply the same mammoth fixes as for the arrival (dark fur, distinct trunk, head hump, shaggy fringe). Give the sledge darker #533d30 runners and two pale bundles.

problems: The gatherer's grass cape reads as narrow smooth panels rather than a constructed layer of woven vegetation.
The gathering basket resembles a smooth cylindrical pail, making the material and occupation less specific.
Proportions and clothing read. The two figures differ in hair and outfit
The stone adze is a tiny dark block at hip level and doesn't register
The right figure's green grass cape is narrow and mostly hidden, and the basket hangs low in front of the knees and reads as floating
elements.fix: Preserve both supplied blocky bodies and the 44-part total. Form the cape from broad overlapping grass panels with an uneven hem over the hide skirt, and give the basket a squat faceted body, thick fibre rim and flexible-looking loop handle; keep the other resident's lashed stone adze and unequal fur boots clearly exposed. / Make the adze 0.7 m long: a pale #c3a575 handle with a 0.25 m grey #81847a stone head, held up in the hand at shoulder height. Widen the grass cape to 0.6 m across the shoulders and lengthen it to the hips in #a8ad68 with a #526b40 hem. Move the basket so its rim is under the hand at y ~0.9 and add a 0.06 m handle strap from the hand to the rim.

problems: The roof reads as broad flat rectangular panels on regular straight posts, giving the shelter a modern pavilion-like construction.
The matching straight orange seats look like cut beams rather than gathered fallen logs.
The shelter roof is three flat, crisp-edged rectangular boards in neat rows. It reads as a sawn-timber pergola, not 'a hide shelter'.
There are 11 flat green and yellow-green discs of 1.6–2.8 m scattered around the base, which read as floating lily pads or decorative mats rather than ground cover.
The hearth with broth pot, stone slab and log seats are good.
The roof is two flat rectangular brown slabs that read as milled planks or a picnic shelter, which contradicts 'no machine-cut lumber'
Half a dozen bright flat green discs around the edge look like lily pads or pancakes
The broth pot and bowls on the stone slab are small, so 'serving warm broth' doesn't read, and nothing says 'café' rather than 'lean-to with fire'

World rule: centrepiece hierarchy: add a rule that the square bonfire is the largest fire in the age, with flames 1.4–1.6 m and a vertical Chief's marker post. Every other fire (café hearth, home fire ring, camp fire) must stay under 0.6 m of flame and under 1.5 m across, so the centrepiece reads as the town centre.
World rule: avoid: add 'flat rectangular plank roofs or plank seat strips' (café roof, bench top). Stone Age roofs are sagging hide panels on crooked poles, or bark/thatch.
elements.fix: Make the roof visibly stretched hide with sagging uneven edges, overlapping patches and oversized sinew ties on crooked forked poles. Replace the matched beams with unequal broad split logs around the broth hearth, keeping bowls on low rough supports rather than introducing a sales counter. / Replace the three roof boards with 2–3 sagging hide panels (each 2 slabs at slightly different tilts, #987052/#c3a575 with a darker #76513b patch) stretched over crooked poles, with pole ends sticking out 0.3 m past the hide. Add a smoke-hole gap. Cut the ground discs to 3–4, recolour them to match the meadow (#7c9254/#687b46), and make them irregular by overlapping 2 flattened spheres each. / Replace the roof slabs with a stretched-hide awning: 3–4 overlapping tilted hide panels (#b7976c/#e1d3ae) that sag between 4 crooked poles, with pale lashings at the corners. Delete the green discs. Make the cooking pot 0.8 m (dark #3b2a22) on a visible tripod over glowing embers. Line up 5–6 large pale bowls (0.3 m, #e1d3ae with #c88343 broth tops) on the slab, and put 2 log seats facing the slab so it reads as a serving counter.

problems: The rock-and-log translation is appropriate, but the silhouette resolves into thin scaffolding against stacked rounded boulders.
Occupied rooms, load-bearing contacts and usable ladder landings are difficult to distinguish at stream distance.

The stepped rock-and-log tower is a strong idea, but the four platforms are flat sawn decks (#b7976c/#c3a575 boxes with crisp edges), and the climbing ladders have evenly spaced rungs on two parallel rails. These read as modern lumber and ladders.
The whole rock pile is a symmetric cone from base to summit, like a stacked sandcastle, rather than a natural outcrop the clan has built into.

World rule: avoid list: add 'flat sawn boards and decks, two-rail ladders with even rungs, post-and-rail fence segments'. Roofs and platforms must be lashed round poles or sagging hide; climbing uses notched logs.
elements.fix: Consolidate the tower into a few broad stepped rock terraces with chunky braced log spans visibly bearing on ledges. Group hide-clad rooms into readable masses and provide one clear staggered ladder route with generous landings; reduce thin rail-like clutter while retaining the footprint and tall clan-lodging skyline. / Replace each deck box with 4–5 lashed round poles side by side (cylinders 0.2 m, slightly different lengths) with hide ties, plus a hide awning over each cave mouth instead of a flat roof board. Replace the ladders with single notched climbing logs (one thick cylinder tilted 0.4 rad, with 3–4 small offset notches) or rope-and-branch ladders with crooked uneven rungs. Shift the upper rock masses 0.8–1.2 m off-axis toward −x so the outcrop leans and is lopsided.

problems: The bonfire is the right idea (no fountain), but in the vignette it is roughly the same size and silhouette as the café's hearth and the home's fire ring. It reads as 'another campfire', not the Chief's communal centre of the town.
The stone ring is small and tightly packed, the flames are under about 1 m, and the three log seats are short and close in. The whole thing covers maybe 2.5 m of a large square.
No vertical element marks it as the place the town gathers around.

World rule: centrepiece hierarchy: add a rule that the square bonfire is the largest fire in the age, with flames 1.4–1.6 m and a vertical Chief's marker post. Every other fire (café hearth, home fire ring, camp fire) must stay under 0.6 m of flame and under 1.5 m across, so the centrepiece reads as the town centre.
elements.fix: Spread the piece to the full 4.5 m diameter. Use 10–12 boulders (0.5–0.8 m, #81847a/#a49b80) in a broken ring with a 1 m entrance gap. Add 4 long logs 2.5 m leaning together in a tipi frame over the fire, plus 2 fallen logs. Raise the flame wedges to 1.4–1.6 m, still broad (no taller), with orange #f07835 outer and yellow #e9b04c inner. Lengthen the three seat logs to 2 m and move them out to a 3.5 m radius. Add one Chief's marker post 2.8 m tall at the back of the ring, topped with an antler pair and an ochre-painted hide, so it is unmistakably the town's centre. Shrink the other pieces' fires (see bibleChanges).

problems: The hood is a cream box enclosing the whole head with no visible face. It reads as a box helmet or beekeeper hood.
The 'unfamiliar clan emblem' on the bundle is a teal ring that reads as a roll of tape or a modern plastic ring.
The patchwork fur wrap reads as a flat tan tunic with no shaggy edge.
The head is fully wrapped in cream hood boxes and has no eyes or features, so it reads as a blank block or robot head
The shell necklace is a row of white balls across the chest, like buttons
The hooked staff curls the wrong way and reads as a cane handle sticking off the side
elements.fix: Open the hood to a cowl framing a visible skin-tone face (hood boxes only on the top, back and sides, #76513b weathered hide). Add 3 drooping fur-edge flaps (#987052/#533d30) at the hem and shoulders, in patchwork colours. Replace the teal ring with a painted hide disc (#e1d3ae) carrying an ochre/charcoal spiral or zigzag emblem. Keep the shell beads; they work. / Open the hood front: pull the side panels back so the tan face shows, and add two dark eye boxes (0.07 m) and a beard or charcoal mark. Recolour the hood a darker weathered #8a7a66 so it contrasts with the cream shells. Make the shells larger and fewer (5 at 0.22 m) on a visible #3b2a22 cord hung in a V. Make the staff 2.2 m with a clear shepherd's hook at the top, curling forward over the head.

problems: The stake uses #987052, the same as the road's accent colour, so at stream scale the stake vanishes against the mud and the flame floats
The flame cluster (~1.3 m) reads well, but the whole torch is only ~3.5 m and thin. In the vignette it is a tiny orange tick
The pale hide bindings are tiny and the fork is not readable
World rule: lighting: wood must contrast with the road. Forbid using the road colours #76513b/#987052 for the torch stake; use #3b2a22, or peeled #c3a575 with dark bindings.
elements.fix: Recolour the stake to dark #3b2a22, or peeled pale #c3a575 with dark bindings, so it contrasts with both the mud and the moss. Thicken it to 0.4 m. Scale the flame cones 1.3x and add one low #ffd075 glow core. Make the resin bundle a chunky 0.5 m #533d30 wrap with two #e1d3ae hide bands, each 0.12 m tall.

problems: The tall black-and-brown feather dominates the headdress. The antler pair is thin (0.11 m tines) and the same cream as the collar, so the 'branched antlers' read weakly
The pale fur collar cylinder rings the face, so the head looks like it is in a white ruff
The staff is a thin dark pole whose bone top is a small cream cube
elements.fix: Double the thickness of the antler beams and tines (0.2 m) and spread them wider (tips at x ±0.8, y 2.7). Make them asymmetric (one side has an extra tine). Darken the collar to #b7976c and lower it to the shoulders. Thicken the staff to 0.18 m and top it with a 0.45 m skull-like bone shape (box plus two horn cones) with a #c88343 ochre wrap below.
